grand_strategy.reading: Canada is a middle power whose security and market both point south, and whose largest partner is now its coercer. Ottawa answers with a deliberate turn to Europe, Britain, Asia and the Arctic while keeping NORAD, CUSMA and NATO, the frame it cannot afford to lose. The turn is transactional by design, from the China EV quota to the India uranium deal, and the grades say so: partner with most of them, reluctant only where the alignment is new. Every hedge that answers Washington also gives it a target, so the test is whether the annual CUSMA reviews stay talk or become the exit.

stances.note: Read from Ottawa, the same pair as the USA card: NORAD and NATO partner, kin in language, border and history, and a coercive Washington. Canada grades the US reluctant_ally rather than partner because the security structure (NORAD, NATO, the Arctic) is still shared while the trade and the 51st-state line are openly hostile. Cooling: the 35% IEEPA tariffs, the Section 338 duty of 50% on about USD 20bn of goods from 22 August 2026, the CUSMA left unrenewed on 1 July 2026, and Carney's own statement that he has planned for a US invasion (NYT, September 2026). Mirror: the USA card reads the pair as reluctant_ally cooling, bond kin, the same sources.

Reluctant_ally and not rival by the co-member rule; the structure (NORAD, NATO, over 70% of Canadian exports) is untouched while the posture is coercive; Carney told the NYT he has planned for a US invasion. Cooling. Bond - kin: the 51st-state claim is itself a kinship claim; language, border, history. Canada has no card yet; its own side will be written in the reverse pass.
